note: Fits the surface profile and fails the substance. On successful he plausibly qualifies — flexible laptop-based work, visits clients and other companies, and runs a clothing line ("We designed some clothes") — though he never states a role or ownership, so this is inferred and soft. On not_deconditioned he clears the exclusion as written: he is not gym-averse at all, trains circuits, does spinning classes and has walked over 10,000 steps a day for three years. He fails neglected_health outright — this is not a neglected area, it is an active medical crisis with an HbA1c that hit 100 against a scale where his endocrinologist said "the maximum we see is 120", plus a grade 2 spondylolisthesis and an arthritic post-surgical knee. He fails good_to_great just as clearly: this is rescue, not optimisation, in his own words "To be honest, I want my life back" and "I feel a lot of waste has happened", from a peak bodyweight around 150 kg. Income could not be assessed at all — no price was named and finances were never discussed — so it is recorded in neither list. The pattern this call adds to the corpus is that the stated ICP's lack of any clinical criterion again does the damage: the prospect is commercially plausible and personally motivated, and the thing that actually disqualifies him is a body and a disease the ICP does not screen for.
